Print a TITE-BOIN Decision Table

Source: R/print.tite_boin_decision_table.R
print.tite_boin_decision_table.Rd

Display the decision table produced by tite_boin_decision_table in the layout of the published tables: one row per number of patients treated, number of DLTs and range of pending patients sharing a decision, with the boundaries on the follow-up statistic in the Escalate, Stay and De-escalate columns.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'tite_boin_decision_table'
print(x, cohort_size = NULL, digits = 2, ...)

Arguments

x

An object of class tite_boin_decision_table.

cohort_size

Integer scalar or NULL. When supplied, only the sample sizes that are multiples of cohort_size are shown, which is how the published tables are laid out.

digits

Integer scalar. Number of decimal places of the boundaries. Defaults to 2, as in the published tables.

...

Further arguments, currently ignored.

Value

The object x, invisibly.

Details

A boundary shown as ">= 2.15" under Escalate means that the dose is escalated when the follow-up statistic is at least 2.15; the statistic is STFT for method = "imputation" and ESS for method = "ess". "Suspend if >= 4.23" under Escalate marks an escalation blocked by min_completed. When the table was built with a positive min_follow_up, an escalation with pending patients carries the condition on MF, for example ">= 0.22 & MF >= 0.25"; accrual is suspended when the condition on the follow-up statistic holds but the one on MF does not.

A data frame that no longer has the columns or attributes of a decision table, for example after selecting columns, is printed as a plain data frame.

See also

tite_boin_decision_table, plot.tite_boin_decision_table

Examples

decisions <- tite_boin_decision_table(target = 0.3, max_n = 15)

# Table S1 of Yuan et al. (2018)
print(decisions, cohort_size = 3)
#> TITE-BOIN decision table with target 0.3
#> Method: single mean imputation (Yuan et al., 2018); boundaries refer to STFT
#> 
#>  Patients DLTs Pending Escalate Stay    De-escalate

#>  6        >= 4 <= 2                     Y & Elim   
#>  9        0    <= 4    Y                           
#>  9        0    >= 5    Suspend  Suspend Suspend

#>  9        1    >= 5    Suspend  Suspend Suspend

#>  15       3    3       >= 1.29  < 1.29

# Boundaries with three decimal places
print(decisions[decisions$n == 9, ], digits = 3)
